title: Northstar Relay
description: A small software company that automates large operational data exports, as of 21 August 2026. Four customers, one export incident holding a renewal, one release with a late decision in it, and an engineer starting on Monday.

northstar.description: Everything the company knows about itself: its people and projects, the exports it runs for its customers, the money, and the conversation.

organizations.description: Northstar Relay, its four customers, and its two suppliers.

people.description: Everyone at Northstar, and the contact at each customer and supplier.

customers.description: The four subscriptions, what each one pays, and who to talk to.

projects.description: The four pieces of work in flight in late August.

tasks.description: Every task in those projects, with its status, owner and due date.

repositories.description: The three services the product is built from.

issues.description: Open issues, including the export timeout behind the Lumen incident.

support_cases.description: The two cases support is carrying.

supplier_bills.description: Twelve months of compute and office costs.

ledger_entries.description: The double-entry record behind every invoice, payment and bill.

export_runs.description: Six months of export jobs -- the product's own operational record.

calendar_events.description: The three meetings that decide this week.

chat_messages.description: What the team said in general, lumen-renewal and release-2-8.

email_messages.description: The mail behind the invoices and the incident.

documents.description: The renewal brief and Theo's first-week plan.

scheduled_export_timeouts.title: Scheduled exports that timed out
scheduled_export_timeouts.description: Every scheduled run stopped by the legacy 120-second worker limit, newest first. This is the incident behind the Lumen Labs renewal.
scheduled_export_timeouts.sql:
select date(started_at) as day, customer_id, row_count, duration_s, failure_reason
from export_runs
where status = 'failed'
order by started_at desc

export_volume_by_month.title: Export volume by customer, by month
export_volume_by_month.description: How much data each account moves, and how fast that is changing.
export_volume_by_month.sql:
select substr(started_at, 1, 7) as month, customer_id,
       count(*) as runs, sum(row_count) as rows_exported
from export_runs
group by 1, 2
order by 1 desc, 4 desc

open_work.title: Open work, and who has it
open_work.description: Every task that is not done, with the person carrying it.
open_work.sql:
select projects.name as project, tasks.title, tasks.status, tasks.priority,
       assignee.name as assignee, tasks.due_on
from tasks
join projects on projects.id = tasks.project_id
left join people as assignee on assignee.id = tasks.assignee_person_id
where tasks.status != 'done'
order by case tasks.priority when 'urgent' then 0 when 'high' then 1 else 2 end,
         tasks.due_on

time_logged.title: Time logged, by person
time_logged.description: Everything booked against a task, newest first.
time_logged.sql:
select time_entries.date, people.name as person, tasks.title as task,
       time_entries.minutes, time_entries.note
from time_entries
join people on people.id = time_entries.person_id
join tasks on tasks.id = time_entries.task_id
order by time_entries.date desc, people.name

money_owed.title: Invoices that are still open
money_owed.description: What has been billed and not yet paid.
money_owed.sql:
select number, customer_id, description, issued_on, due_on, amount_usd, status
from invoices
where status != 'paid'
order by due_on

monthly_books.title: Invoiced against supplier costs, by month
monthly_books.description: Subscription billing next to what the company paid out.
monthly_books.sql:
select months.month,
       (select round(sum(amount_usd), 2) from invoices
         where substr(issued_on, 1, 7) = months.month) as invoiced,
       (select round(sum(amount_usd), 2) from supplier_bills
         where substr(issued_on, 1, 7) = months.month) as supplier_costs
from (select distinct substr(issued_on, 1, 7) as month from invoices) as months
order by months.month desc
